process_area.title: Pricing, Promotion, Loyalty & Payment Integrity Monitoring

value_stream.name: Revenue Assurance, Pricing Integrity & Leakage Management

fields.Participants: Revenue Assurance Lead, Merchandising/Pricing (links to VS-01.2), POS/IT (links to VS-08), Store Ops (links to VS-07), Loss Prevention (links to VS-23), BI (links to VS-28.1)
fields.Trigger: Near-real-time POS events; daily exception report

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-monitor of "monitor shelf-price vs system-price vs charged-price integrity" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-detect of "Revenue Assurance Lead/Store Ops monitor price-override and manual-price-entry integrity" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-count of "discounting/under-ringing, drive corrective action" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-584 (ensure controlled execution — Pricing, Promotion, Loyalty & Payment Integrity Monitoring (PA-118.2).)
- operational: price-integrity monitoring; operational: override analytics and thresholds
Pain Points / Risks: - **Shelf/system mismatch risk**: Customer charged wrong price (under or over); mitigated by price-integrity monitoring
- **Override-abuse risk**: Manual overrides used to under-charge (collusion); mitigated by override analytics and thresholds
System Touchpoints: - Price master (links to VS-01.2/VS-29); POS (links to VS-08); exception reporting (links to VS-23.1); BI (links to VS-28.1); store ops (links to VS-07)

steps.activity: Revenue Assurance Lead monitor shelf-price vs system-price vs charged-price integrity: confirm the price actually charged at POS matches the approved retail/trade/corporate/promo price master (links to VS-01.2/VS-29), detect shelf-label-vs-system price mismatches, and investigate systematic under-ringing

Revenue Assurance Lead/Store Ops monitor price-override and manual-price-entry integrity: audit override frequency by cashier/store, flag excessive/depth overrides, detect "sale-no-stock" and zero-price anomalies, and investigate potential collusion/sweethearting (links to VS-23.1/W842)
steps.r: Revenue Assurance Lead / Store Ops / Loss Prevention

steps.activity: Revenue Assurance Lead quantify pricing-leakage: estimate revenue lost to mis-pricing/over-discounting/under-ringing, drive corrective action (price-lock, override thresholds, cashier coaching), and feed to leak-detection (W3705) and pricing governance (links to VS-01.2)

fields.Participants: Revenue Assurance Lead, Promotions/Marketing (links to VS-58/VS-14), Merchandising (links to VS-01.2), POS/IT (links to VS-08), Ecommerce (links to VS-10), Loyalty (links to VS-13), BI (links to VS-28.1)
fields.Volume: 6 major catalog promos/yr + monthly hot deals + bundle/loyalty-exclusive (profile §13.3)

- System auto-count of "discount/markdown integrity during the event" (replaces manual Step 2).

- operational: pre-event verification; operational: stacking limits and monitoring
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mis-configured-promo risk**: Promo applies wrong discount (over-discount = revenue loss); mitigated by pre-event verification
- **Stacking-abuse risk**: Customers/cashiers stack promos beyond intent; mitigated by stacking limits and monitoring
System Touchpoints: - Promotions (links to VS-58); merchandising/pricing (links to VS-01.2); POS/ecommerce (links to VS-08/VS-10); loyalty (links to VS-13); markdown budget (links to VS-101); vendor co-op (links to VS-39); BI (links to VS-28.1)

steps.activity: Revenue Assurance Lead/Promotions assure promotion setup integrity before and during events: verify the promo mechanism (BOGO, % off, bundle price, quantity break) is configured correctly in POS/ecommerce, the eligible items/dates/conditions are right, and the promo applies the intended discount (not more/less)

Revenue Assurance Lead monitor discount/markdown integrity during the event: detect discount-stacking abuse (multiple promos combining beyond intent), over/under-discounting, promo application to ineligible items, and expired promo still live; investigate anomalies (links to W1475 coupon abuse)

Revenue Assurance Lead reconcile promo/markdown cost: reconcile promo discount given vs budgeted (links to VS-101 markdown budget/VS-39 vendor co-op funding), recover vendor-funded promo where applicable, and report promo-integrity and leakage to merchandising (links to VS-01.2) and leak-detection (W3705)

fields.Frequency: Rare as a *mass* event; ~2–5 events/year chain-wide cross the threshold (single-SKU label errors are the W3697 daily-detection steady state, not this workflow)
fields.Participants: Merchandising Pricing Team (the W13 price-file execution canon owner), IT Platform (price-file pipeline ESB/integration), Store Operations (re-label execution via the W63 task channel), VP Legal / Compliance (RA 7581 Price Act / Consumer Act exposure), Customer Service (refund handling per W1622 tiers), Finance Controller (margin impact), DTI liaison (per W427 regulatory-desk pattern), Corporate Communications (if consumer-facing)
fields.Trigger: A bad price-file push is detected — POS/ESL/shelf-label prices deviating from the approved price master beyond threshold (W3697 monitoring alarm, a store's shelf-label audit exception, a customer DTI complaint, or a margin-variance spike) — affecting > 50 SKUs or > 1 store
fields.Volume: 1 event × affected SKUs × affected stores × exposure duration (units sold in the mispriced window from POS data — the quantification base in Step 5); worst-case scenario: a master-to-store propagation error touching all 200 stores

workflows.name: Price-File Integrity Event Response & Mass-Mispricing Rollback

Automation Opportunity: - Mass-deviation detector: W3697 alert data auto-triggers this workflow's case with the blast-radius scope pre-computed (SKUs × stores × window) (replaces manual Step 1 scoping)
- Re-label campaign auto-tracks per-store completion with label-count reconciliation and escalates stragglers at 24 h (replaces manual Step 3 tracking)
- Refund-difference calculator pre-fills service-desk refunds from POS evidence in the exposure window (replaces manual Step 4 lookups)
Background: The pricing surfaces are individually owned: W13 executes price-file changes, W3697 monitors override/accuracy integrity, W3698 watches promotion integrity, and VS-57 watches competitive/stale prices — but no workflow owned the *event*: confirming a mass deviation, deciding the customer-exposure posture (overcharge vs undercharge), executing a rollback through the W13 canon with a re-label sweep across stores, remediating overcharged customers, quantifying the margin leak, and handling a DTI complaint. The regulatory stakes are specific: RA 7581 (Price Act) SRP-mandated SKUs and the Consumer Act's price-tag regime expose the company to DTI enforcement even when the deviation was an innocent systems error, and an overcharge window is a refund obligation while an undercharge window is an unrecoverable margin leak (goodwill policy governs, not clawback). This workflow is the event canon; detection stays with W3697, rollback execution always rides W13, POS refund mechanics stay W1622/W1538.
Controls: - CTL-584 (ensure controlled execution — Pricing, Promotion, Loyalty & Payment Integrity Monitoring (PA-118.2).)
- operational: no chain-wide price-file push resumes after a mass-deviation event until the canary-store verification passes under the W13 canon
- operational: every confirmed overcharge window produces a quantified refund liability and a remediation register entry reviewed by the Controller
Pain Points / Risks: - **Regulatory risk**: SRP-mandated SKU violations draw DTI notices even for innocent errors; mitigated by the Step-2 triage placing SRP SKUs first in triage, rollback priority, and the Step-6 evidence-pack response

- **Propagation risk**: the fix itself re-propagates the error because the pipeline fault persists; mitigated by the change-control freeze (Step 1) and canary-store verification before chain-wide release (Step 3)

- **Remediation-parity risk**: overcharged customers without receipts or loyalty identity go unremediated; mitigated by the price-difference honor policy and proactive outreach to loyalty-identifiable purchasers (Step 4)
- **Quantification risk**: the window start is wrong (first affected push mis-dated), understating both refunds and leakage; mitigated by the W13 file-log timestamp reconstruction in Step 1
- **Recurrence risk**: root cause fixed but the pipeline lacks a gate; mitigated by the Step-7 pre-push diff gate and mass-deviation detector
Staffing Implication: - Absorbed within Revenue Assurance, Merchandising pricing, IT platform and existing store labor; the re-label sweep uses the same store-task labor pool as planogram resets (VS-55). No incremental headcount.
System Touchpoints: - Price-master vs staged-file diff report & change-control freeze switch on the price-file pipeline (links to W13 execution canon)
- W13 file-push log with canary-store verification states & POS/ESL sync telemetry
- Re-label task campaign via the W63 store-task channel with per-store completion confirmation
- POS refund transactions & service-desk cases (links to W1622/W1538); loyalty goodwill-point adjustments
- Revenue-leakage register & recovery analytics (links to VS-118.1/W118.3)
- DTI response desk file: exhibits & correspondence (links to W658 pattern; VS-88 document control)
Time Estimate: Per event: Steps 1–3 ≈ 40–120 staff-hours across Revenue Assurance, IT and store labor (a 200-store re-label sweep is the dominant term — ~20–60 store-hours per store at full scope); Steps 4–6 ≈ 40–160 staff-hours over the remediation fortnight; event-driven, no annual figure claimed. Steady-state sensor cost stays in W3697's daily detection.

steps.activity: **Confirm & contain**: reproduce the deviation (staged vs master price comparison per SKU/store); localize the fault — master-data error, pipeline transform error, or store-sync failure; **freeze further price-file pushes** (change-control hold with IT) to stop propagating; scope the blast radius: SKUs × stores × window start (first affected push timestamp from the W13 file log)

**Exposure & regulatory triage**: split the SKU set — overcharged vs undercharged vs SRP-mandated (RA 7581 list); VP Legal assesses DTI exposure (SRP violations are strict-liability notices even if accidental) and the conspicuous-error defense posture for undercharges; if a DTI complaint already arrived, the W658-pattern response desk opens with the corrected master and sync logs as exhibits

**Rollback & re-label sweep**: corrected file executes through the W13 canon (approve → distribute → verify POS/ESL sync at canary stores, then chain-wide); Store Operations issues the re-label task via the W63 channel with priority order: SRP-mandated SKUs, promo-endcap zones, high-velocity SKUs, then the tail; completion confirmed per store (label-count vs SKU-count match)

**Customer remediation**: overcharge window — refund the difference at the service desk on receipt/loyalty-lookup evidence (W1622 approval tiers; W1538 refund mechanics), proactive outreach for loyalty-identifiable purchasers, price-difference honor policy published if consumer-facing; undercharge window — no clawback beyond the conspicuous-error/legal posture Legal set in Step 2; goodwill points per the loyalty policy where brand damage occurred

**Financial quantification**: compute exposure = Σ (price delta × units sold in window) per SKU/store from POS data; classify overcharge refunds (liability set aside per Controller) vs undercharge margin leak (revenue-leakage register per the VS-118.1 framework); feed the leakage-recovery analytics (W118.3)

**Regulatory close-out**: respond to any DTI notice within deadline — corrective-evidence pack (master price history, push logs, rollback timestamps, remediation totals); compliance visit handled per the W658 inspection-response pattern; follow-up undertakings tracked to closure

**Root-cause & pipeline hardening**: post-mortem with IT and Merchandising — pre-push validation gate (master-vs-staged automated diff, zero-tolerance on SRP-mandated SKUs), canary-store push stage added to the W13 execution canon, W3697 alert thresholds tightened (mass-deviation detector: > N SKUs deviating in one store-day); runbook updated; report to the revenue-assurance governance forum
